title: Traffic slicing canvas + edge fallback playbook (draft)
content:
Context: quick working draft for a combined 'traffic slicing' UI canvas that surfaces canary/A-B routing + automatic fallback policies for inference routes. Goal is a single view product managers and platform engineers can use to define experiments, simulate traffic, and encode guardrails without touching infra config files. This is intentionally rough; focus on flows and open questions.

High-level product goals
- Make it trivial to run small, safe canaries and A/B tests (0.1% -> 100%) with observable safety nets.
- Encourage routing-by-policy (cost, latency, quality) rather than hardwired endpoints.
- Reduce burn and outages by making automatic fallback policies configurable and understandable to non-SREs.

Primary UX surfaces proposed
1) Canvas view (center): a timeline + traffic-slice chart showing percent by variant over time. Drag handles to set ramp schedule (start, pause, cadence). Live metric overlays: 99th latency, error rate, prompt-quality delta (from eval set).
2) Variant cards (left column): model variant, weight, target audience (user segments or IP range), annotations (owner, changelog link), quick actions (pause, promote, rollback).
3) Policy builder (right column): human-readable conditional rules (if latency > 1200ms for 5m AND error_rate > 1% -> fallback to variant X). Support precedence and OR/AND groups. Include numeric knobs for lookback windows and smoothing.
4) Simulation mode: replay historical traffic slice to see estimated cost and predicted SLO hit. Toggle to run test traffic (sandboxed) for up to N tokens.
5) Audit trail & replay: store events (deploy, ramp, policy-trigger) and allow event replay to debug. Expose linked logs/trace ids to APM.

Wireframe notes / microcopy suggestions
- Canvas title: "Staged deployments — traffic slicing"
- Variant card header: "Variant: gptx-16q (quantized) — canary"
- Policy toggle: "Auto-fallback: ON — will fail open to baseline when triggered"
- Safety banner (when rule armed): "This policy will automatically reroute traffic if thresholds breach — verify targets before ramping > 5%"
- Empty state copy: "No active rollouts. Create a canary or import a rollout policy. Tip: start at 0.5% and let automatic checks run for 30m before increasing."

Acceptance criteria (draft)
- Users can create a rollout that ramps from 0.1% to 20% on a defined schedule and attach at least one auto-fallback policy.
- The canvas must show metric overlays and a clear state when a policy has been triggered.
- Simulation must produce an estimated 95% CI for cost and SLO impact.
- Audit trail lists policy triggers with links to traces and the exact decision conditions.

Open design/engineering questions
- Where does policy evaluation run? Edge (serving nodes) or control plane? (Tradeoff: faster local response vs. consistency across nodes).
- How to surface "quality" regressions? We have eval sets but they can be noisy. Suggest: require two signals (quality delta + downstream user metric change) before auto-fallback to avoid flapping.
- Default thresholds: should we offer opinionated defaults (latency 2x baseline, errors > 1%)? If so, we need strong docs and an onboarding checklist.
- Role controls: who can create a global auto-fallback? Team leads only? Suggest role gating for policy edit, but allow engineers to create non-global experiments.

Edge cases to cover in backlog
- Nested rollouts: two rollouts targeting overlapping user segments — precedence rules and visual conflict resolution.
- Multi-route fallbacks: fallback target unavailable -> cascade to next compatible variant. Need to show where traffic will end up.
- Metric missingness: if telemetry pipeline lags, policies should have a "stale data" behavior (pause ramp or rely on error/latency only).
- Canary warmup: some models need warm KV caches — show expected increased latency during first N minutes and differentiate that from real regressions.

Proposed backlog tickets (examples)
- ROLL-300: Canvas timeline interactions + drag-to-ramp UX (owner: Priya)
- ROLL-307: Policy editor with AND/OR groups and lookback windows (owner: Marco)
- ROLL-319: Simulation mode backend + UI (owner: Diego)
- ROLL-325: Audit trail schema + trace linking (owner: eng-sre)

Telemetry & alerting integration notes
- Policy triggers should create an incident draft (low noise) with automatic links to traces, recent changes, and responsible owner.
- Expose per-rollout dashboards with token cost, served requests, latency percentiles, and custom eval metrics.
- Add a lightweight health signal that marks a rollout as "unstable" when multiple policies fire within X hours.

Accessibility + internationalization
- Ensure timeline controls are keyboard accessible and provide numeric inputs for exact percent + time.
- All microcopy needs i18n keys; default English copy must be concise to fit narrow sidebars.

Prototype flows to test in user research (next steps)
1) Launch a 0.5% canary with auto-fallback on latency only — observe if PMs understand the timeline and policy trigger explanation.
2) Set up an A/B test with two model variants for a subset of users and validate that analytic dashboards match expected buckets.
3) Run simulation on a historical spike to ensure the UI explains why predicted SLOs worsen.

Next steps (short-term)
- Wireframe a low-fidelity Figma for the canvas + policy builder (Priya, by 2024-12-06).
- Groom the above backlog tickets into an initial sprint (sprint lead: Marco) and create engineering spike for policy evaluation location.
- Run a brief feedback session with SRE and solutions-eng teams to validate fallback semantics (invite list: eng-sre, solutions-eng, product).

Notes to reviewers
- This intentionally mixes UX and policy semantics; feedback should call out anything that looks operationally unsafe.
- If you have strong opinions about precedence (rollout-level vs global policy), add a short rationale in the comment thread (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CHX12345).

Quick links (for reviewer convenience)
- Canary policy primer (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROLL/Canary+policy+primer
- Existing rollout code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-service
- Discussion thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CHX12345/p1700000000

— Asha
